name: systematic-debugging
adaptations: Shortened workflow; redacted diagnostics; scoped testing and authorization; removed plugin dependencies and arbitrary escalation threshold.

name: verification-before-completion
adaptations: Allows valid unchanged evidence reuse; distinguishes focused proof from full completion; preserves final-head review requirements. Matches cost claims to complete workloads, requires timeout diagnosis before budget changes, and treats delegated audit results as scoped evidence. Adds a conditional contract-evidence gate for cross-boundary changes: independent identity channels, source/cache proof, comparable measurements, independent coverage audit, and explicit hold decisions for missing evidence.

name: tdd
adaptations: Infers authorized test boundaries; permits contract-relevant durable state and forbidden-call assertions; avoids forced approvals and unavailable skill dependencies. Adds ordered-history corruption cases and complete-operation growth checks for relevant workloads, preserving cache correctness and avoiding universal scale-test requirements. Covers lifecycle phases through durable completion and tests cancellation through the owning runtime or transport, preserving required accounting and committed decisions.

name: property-based-testing
adaptations: Focused state and boundary testing; Go standard-library option; no compulsory dependency or refactoring.

name: variant-analysis
adaptations: Self-contained direct workflow; no compulsory delegation, plugin command, report template, or CI rule. Includes repeated-operation and reader/writer coverage for cost defects, revisits exclusions after recurring findings, and limits audit claims to inspected paths. Extends lifecycle analysis across owners, phases, and distinct stop causes while distinguishing required bookkeeping and previously committed decisions from fresh admission.

name: security-best-practices
adaptations: Preserves existing authorization, threat-model format, and independent review policy. Replaces broad copied security handbooks with focused Go/browser guidance checked against official Go, WHATWG, and W3C sources. Corrects process execution, HTTP defaults, CORS, event handlers, CSP, opaque-origin messaging, and mandatory-tool overreach.

name: watch
adaptations: Codex-compatible video analysis and document guidance; adapts frame selection and VTT parsing for short/long cues. Read-only preflight with explicit unsupported-Python/missing-executable/enabled-Deno reasons across output modes, optional local audio extraction independent of frame failures, no installers/configuration keys/cloud uploads. Isolated runs/fetches; HTTPS YouTube hosts; yt-dlp config/plugins/remote components disabled; FFmpeg local input protocols and current timing options. Successful final downloads and validated budgets/ranges. Two-pass capped selection with bounded JPEGs/selection memory, uniform first/last coverage preserved through dedup, and explicit FPS retained in both fallbacks. Half-open caption/cue boundaries, finite positive caption intervals and millisecond precision; identical rolling-cue unions preserve coverage without moving added words earlier. Range-checked decoded timestamps including cue frames, separate requested times, full cue request/omission records and sampling state retained on failure. Saved reports/manifests, sidecar captions, language selection, partial evidence and offline/native tests using built-in MPEG-4/AAC encoders. Remote media admission uses finite sections up to 30 minutes, rejects live/unknown full durations, and downloads admitted ranges with accurate MP4/AAC re-encoding, fine encoder timing, packet flushing, explicit duration/256 MiB output guards, and rejection of oversized/empty/truncated media without full-download fallback. Source offsets preserve frame/cue/audio meaning and downloaded source ranges; malformed/non-finite metadata duration becomes unknown. Known source metadata survives refused/failed media passes and every remote caption range respects the known source end. A shared display boundary visibly encodes C0/C1/DEL controls in reports/transcripts/parser errors/tool logs/media diagnostics, requests UTF-8 Python output, streams logs in bounded chunks with invalid-byte replacement, and preserves machine/source evidence with JSON escapes. Media-output guards do not cap total transport bytes/time or captions/metadata.
